title: CONDA Condensed Deep Association Learning for Co-Salient Object Detection

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Eq. (10) defines \(\hat F_{s-1,l}=C_3(F_{s-1,l}+U(F_s^A))\), while \(U\) is explicitly only bilinear upsampling. Earlier, the paper defines \(F_s^A\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times H_s\times W_s\times C_s}\) and VGG features \(F_{s-1,l}\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times H_{s-1}\times W_{s-1}\times C_{s-1}}\). For VGG-16, stage 4 has 512 channels and stage 3 has 256 channels. Thus, at the stated stage-4-to-stage-3 enhancement, the addition attempts to add a 512-channel tensor to a 256-channel tensor. A convolution applied only after the addition cannot repair this mismatch. Unlike the decoder fusion, which explicitly includes a projection \(\phi\), Eq. (10) contains no channel projection, so the described operation is not dimensionally executable.

The offset head produces \(\Delta_s^j\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K\times2}\) through a linear layer, so its values are unconstrained real numbers. Equations (13)–(14) add these real offsets to coordinates to form \(n_s^j\), and Eq. (15) then defines the condensed association through direct tensor indexing: \(\tilde a_s^j=a_s^j(n_s^j)\). Direct indexing of a discrete \(H_s\times W_s\) tensor by arbitrary real-valued coordinates is undefined; the equations also provide neither rounding nor differentiable bilinear/grid sampling. Further, there is no clipping, padding, or validity mask for coordinates outside the target-image bounds, which necessarily occurs for windows around border correspondences and can also occur from unrestricted predicted offsets. Therefore the claimed condensation operation is not fully defined as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.1, Eq. (3) and the stated output stages
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states that PAG generates association features only for stages \(s=3,4,5\), and Eq. (3) says \(s\) ranges from 5 to 3. Yet Eq. (3) also performs \(\{\hat F_{s-1,l}\}=\mathrm{Enh}(\{F_{s-1,l}\};F_s^A)\) for every such \(s\). At the final stated iteration \(s=3\), this creates enhanced stage-2 features \(\hat F_{2,l}\). No \(A_2\) or \(F_2^A\) is ever generated, and the decoder definition uses the original \(F_{2,L_2}\), not \(\hat F_{2,L_2}\). Hence this final enhancement has no downstream use under the described architecture. Either the range/last enhancement is wrong, or a stage-2 association/decoder connection is omitted.
